posts.title: AI in Chip Design: From Code Generation to EDA Orchestration (University of Edinburgh)
posts.summary:
Researchers at the University of Edinburgh published a technical perspective titled “LLMs in Digital EDA: A perspective on shifting roles from Generation to Orchestration.” Abstract Excerpt: “In this Perspective, we instead define three hierarchical roles that reveal how capability accumulates: a Generator that produces design artifacts in a single pass, an Agent that refines outputs... » read more
The post AI in Chip Design: From Code Generation to EDA Orchestration (University of Edinburgh) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: A new perspective from the University of Edinburgh categorizes AI in EDA into three roles: Generator, Agent, and Orchestrator.
The research identifies a 'syntax trap' where current models prioritize plausible code generation over physically correct hardware, limiting their utility in industrial design flows.
The authors argue for a shift toward physics-aware orchestrators that can coordinate decisions across multiple EDA stages to improve reliability and scalability.

posts.title: Predicting Thermal Conductivity in Advanced BEOL Interconnect Stacks (Peking University)
posts.summary:
Researchers at Peking University published a technical paper titled “Predictive Structure to Thermal Conductivity Modeling Framework for BEOL Interconnect Stacks in Advanced Technology Nodes Enabled by Extensive Layer Resolved Thermal Measurements.” Abstract Excerpt: “The increasing structural complexity of BEOL interconnect stacks in advanced integrated circuits demands a structure-aware thermal conductivity (κ) modeling framework. However, generalizable... » read more
The post Predicting Thermal Conductivity in Advanced BEOL Interconnect Stacks (Peking University) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers at Peking University developed a structure-aware thermal conductivity modeling framework for BEOL interconnect stacks in advanced technology nodes.
The framework utilizes time-domain thermoreflectance measurements with 100 nm depth resolution to derive empirical relationships between interconnect structure and thermal conductivity.
By incorporating effective medium theory, the model resolves intra-layer 3D thermal distribution, enabling more accurate predictive thermal analysis for 3D ICs.

posts.title: VW launches its first LiDAR-equipped electric SUV in China
posts.summary:
FAW-Volkswagen has launched the ID. AURA T6 electric SUV in China, starting at 129,900 yuan ($19,240) and offering a CLTC range of up to 660 km.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: FAW-Volkswagen has launched the ID. AURA T6, its first all-electric SUV in China to feature LiDAR technology, with pricing starting at 129,900 yuan.
The vehicle utilizes the CEA electronic architecture developed in partnership with Xpeng, supporting advanced features like urban NOA and large AI model deployment.
The integration of Horizon Robotics' chips and Xpeng's software architecture highlights Volkswagen's deepening reliance on local Chinese technology partners to maintain market competitiveness.

posts.title: Epicland X9 to launch on September 24 as first model from Dongfeng-Huawei brand
posts.summary:
The Epicland X9 SUV measures 5,301 mm in length and starts at 299,800 yuan ($44,400) in pre-sales.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Epicland, a joint venture between Dongfeng and Huawei, will officially launch its flagship X9 SUV on September 24, following strong pre-order interest exceeding 20,000 units.
The vehicle features Huawei's Qiankun ADS 5 assisted-driving system and HarmonySpace 6 cockpit, positioning it as a direct competitor to the Aito M9 and Li Auto L9.
The rapid launch of the X9, alongside the upcoming Aistaland GX7, demonstrates the accelerated pace at which Huawei is expanding its automotive partnership ecosystem.

posts.title: Toyota plans China-made extended-range EVs in 2027 to broaden lineup, report says
posts.summary:
Toyota plans to begin EREV production in China in April 2027 and raise output to about 400,000 units in 2028, Nikkei Asia reported.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Toyota plans to enter the Chinese extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) market in April 2027, targeting an annual production capacity of 400,000 units by 2028.
The strategic pivot aims to mitigate the impact of intense price wars in the pure battery electric vehicle (BEV) segment by offering a powertrain that reduces charging infrastructure reliance.
Despite the shift, the EREV segment in China is currently facing headwinds, with retail sales declining 15.85% year-on-year in the first eight months of 2026.
